title: Push the container into bay 2 of the roller deck and lock it in between the raised locks
instruction: Stow the container in bay 2 of the roller deck so it cannot roll back.
context: Ramp agents and air-cargo handlers push ULD containers along the roller decks of dollies and loaders and lock each in place with the deck's flip-up locks; a lock left down lets the container roll back. Done by: cargo agents and freight movers (O*NET 43-5011, 53-7062). Unlike TK-53KLKJ (meter gravity-fed parts with an escapement) and TK-M2TK8E (catch a cart and set its brake), the load is pushed up over a dropped lock and held while the lock is raised behind it.
setup: Positions in cm: x away from the robot, y to the robot's left, from the midpoint between the two arm bases (61 cm apart); heights above the table top. Along the deck, distances are measured from the deck's middle, which is at y = -6.2 (6.2 cm to the robot's right). Roller deck (fixed, dark grey painted steel): a plate 18.0 (x) by 40.0 (along the deck) by 4.5 cm thick, from x = 21.5 to 39.5, sloping 3 degrees down toward the robot's left: its left end rests on the table and its right end on a light grey block 18.0 by 3.0 by 2.0 cm tall under its last 3 cm. Two light grey guide rails 1.0 cm wide and 1.2 cm tall along its whole length, inner faces at x = 24.5 and 36.5, leave a lane 12.0 cm wide centred at x = 30.5. In the lane, 12 aluminium rollers 1.2 cm across and 11.8 cm long, axes along x, tops 2 mm above the deck, four per bay at 1.4 and 4.2 cm either side of each bay's centre. Deck, rollers and container slide at friction 0.02, standing in for free-turning rollers, so the container rolls down the slope by itself. End stops (fixed, black): blocks across the lane, 1.2 cm thick and 1.0 cm above the rollers, inner faces 18.0 cm either side of the deck's middle. Three bays: bay 1 (robot's left, the low end) centred 12.4 cm left of the deck's middle, bay 2 at the middle, bay 3 12.4 cm right; each 11.2 cm long between stop faces. Bay numbers: one, two and three white 1.6 cm squares (2.2 cm apart) on the deck's near strip at x = 22.5, centred on each bay. Two locks (yellow painted steel, 12 g each), 6.2 cm either side of the deck's middle (the 1|2 lock at y = 0): a plate 11.6 cm across the lane and 1.2 cm thick that slides square to the deck through a slot, its top 1.8 cm above the rollers when up; and, in one piece with it, a pedal 2.4 by 2.4 by 1.2 cm at x = 14.0 to 16.4, 5 cm out from the deck's near edge, joined to the plate by a black arm 1.0 cm wide that runs in under the deck; the pedal's top is level with the plate's. Each lock has a push-push catch: pressing its pedal down 2.7 cm or more (3.0 cm is the bottom of travel) drops a raised lock, which then rests with its top 3 mm below the deck; pressing it down again raises it. A light spring (about 0.4 N) holds it at either rest. A raised lock is held rigidly up; only pressing its pedal releases it, so the container cannot push it down. Container (loose, aluminium): a box 10.0 by 10.0 cm and 8.0 cm tall, 1.2 kg, with a 6 by 1 cm blue label band on its face toward the robot; it is wider than the gripper opens (9.4 cm). Lot A (the screenshot): it rests on the rollers of bay 1 against the left end stop, centred at x = 30.5; both locks up. Nothing else is on the table. Lot B: the container rests in bay 3 against the 2|3 lock, and the 1|2 lock is down. Lot C: as lot A, but the 2|3 lock is down. Trials are run on lots A, B and C and averaged; the screenshot shows lot A.
scoring: Measured at the end with a ruler and a photo, and over the trial from the video. Stowed: the container sits on the rollers of bay 2, its underside at most 2 mm off the roller tops and tilted at most 5 degrees from square to the deck, inside the guide rails, its centre at most 1.5 cm from the bay's centre along the deck; both locks either side of bay 2 are up (each within 3 mm of its top); no part of either gripper is within 5 mm of the container or of either lock; and the container is still (under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s). Score 1.0 once stowed has held for 1 s. Score 0 in every other case: the container in bay 1 or bay 3 (including rolled back), in bay 2 with a lock down, part way down or held down, still held or touched, tipped or off the deck. Score 0 for the rest of the trial if at any time the container's underside is more than 1 cm off the rollers (carried over a lock, or tipped onto or over one). Trials are run on each of lots A, B and C and averaged. Possible scores per trial: 0, 1.0.
run_limit: 1,200 steps (60 s at 20 Hz) per trial; three trials (lots A, B and C)
reset_notes: Raise both locks (press a dropped lock's pedal fully until it pops up). Lot A: set the container on the rollers of bay 1; it rolls against the left end stop. Lot B: set it in bay 3; it rolls against the 2|3 lock; then press the 1|2 lock's pedal once so it stays down. Lot C: as lot A, then press the 2|3 lock's pedal once so it stays down. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Approximate. The rollers are a low-friction (0.02) surface on a 3 degree slope, not turning rollers; container and deck are about 1:15 scale. Locks are a plate on a sprung slide with a push-push catch; the rigid hold of a raised lock is a slide limit the simulator lifts only while the pedal is pressed. Three fixed lots, each starting a different set of locks down, stop a fixed routine of presses, not a memorised replay of all three.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (mean of lots A, B and C); demo: 1.0 in each lot
